A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP Thompson sampling study and contain the main text and Appendices A–E. Textual and visual comparison supports reliable matching; all appendix body pages are unchanged after accounting for pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical regret bounds and proofs, including a mathematical two-arm construction. Neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a theoretical paper. Its expanded discussion adds no experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same posterior sampling, maximization, observation, and update steps. Discussion of variance inflation does not introduce an implemented algorithm modification.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical evaluation. The finite-domain and continuous-domain theoretical settings are retained.

E2.justification: GP-UCB and other algorithms remain theoretical comparisons or cited work; neither version reports evaluated baseline methods.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, training budgets, evaluation splits, or testing procedures. The revised mathematical definition in Section 2.3 is a theoretical change.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or case studies. The appendices contain unchanged mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The probabilistic regret guarantees concern theory rather than statistical reporting of experiments.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised, and the stated regret rates are retained. The exponent c2 = 17 highlighted in v2 Section 3.1 was already derived in v1 Appendix A.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces the explicit piecewise-linear interpolation of maximum information gain and its submodularity-based concavity argument with a cited concave upper-bound definition. Section 3.1 also makes the conditional-expectation objection to prior analysis explicit. These are localized mathematical revisions; the principal theorem statements and appendix proof text remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same four principal contributions: the probability-dependent lower bound, second-moment bound, expected lenient-regret bounds, and improved time-horizon dependence. Changing O to Ω in the contribution list aligns that sentence with the lower-bound claim already stated elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly explains why the large exponent c2 = 17 does not establish practical instability, conjectures analogous limitations for algorithms lacking exploration tuning, and qualifies whether variance inflation can repair the analysis in Bayrooti et al.'s setting.

D1.justification: The algorithm specification and posterior-sampling approximation discussion are retained. No implementation settings, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are added or revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds Iwazaki (2026), removes Krause et al. (2008) alongside the interpolation argument, and expands discussion of Takeno et al. (2025a) and Bayrooti et al. (2025a,b). Other bibliography edits largely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Localized additions clarify the introduction, Section 3.1, and the Section 3.4 proof sketch and comparison. Bibliographic cleanup and notation corrections accompany these edits; the overall organization and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from before Section 2.3 on v1 page 6 to before Section 3 on v2 page 7, with accompanying text reflow. No figures or result tables are added, and appendix layouts remain identical apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: v2 usefully clarifies the lower bound's practical implications and qualifies its criticism of prior work. However, Section 2.3 redefines the information-gain interpolant as an upper bound, while unchanged Appendix E still invokes exact equality with the original quantity, notably in Equations (229) and (256). Those equalities no longer follow from the revised definition. This incomplete reconciliation leaves the effect on mathematical reliability unresolved, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
